title: What's New: APIs in E-Documents (2025 release wave 2)

chapters.title: Why APIs for e-documents: flexibility and integration
What is delivered: five APIs and two business events
Demo setup: create e-document from SharePoint
Demo execution: SharePoint to Business Central flow
Demo setup: business event for e-document export
Demo execution: e-document business event and APIs

features.name: E-Documents APIs
features.description: Five new APIs for e-document integration enabling flexible and code-free communication through Power Automate and other tools. Allows triggering processes from e-documents and generating e-documents from external sources.
caveats: Not intended as the first channel of communication
Should be used as parallel or additional channel
E-document file contents must be in base 64 encoding

features.name: E-Document Business Events
features.description: Two business events added for e-document workflows: one that triggers when e-document service status changes, enabling external systems to react to e-document state transitions.
caveats: Specific business event: e document service status changed

features.name: Create E-Document from External Sources
features.description: API capability to generate e-documents in Business Central from various external sources like SharePoint, OneDrive, or other XML sources without manual processing.
caveats: Requires file contents in base 64 encoding
Service must exist in the system

features.name: E-Document Export via Business Events
features.description: Business event capability that detects when e-document service status changes to exported, allowing external systems to retrieve and forward e-documents through alternative channels like email or custom services.
caveats: Condition-based triggering: only fires when status is exported
Requires manual setup of flows in Power Automate or similar tools

features.name: Custom Agents with Copilot Studio Integration
features.description: E-document APIs enable creation of new custom agents using Copilot Studio for orchestrating e-document workflows with AI-driven processes.

quotes.text: So first we wanted to enable flexible and codefree integration.
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes the core design goal of making e-document integration accessible without requiring code

quotes.text: It doesn't mean that it should be first channel of communication. It can be but this is not intended for that.
quotes.why_it_matters: Important limitation: these APIs are meant as supplementary channels, not primary communication paths

quotes.text: it enable your usage and creation of new custom agent using copilot studio because now this is available with APIs
quotes.why_it_matters: Supports the claim that the APIs can be used to build Copilot Studio custom agents.

quotes.text: We deliver five APIs and two business events.
quotes.why_it_matters: Defines the scope of the new e-document integration capability

quotes.text: Important to note is that we expect the contents of a of an electronic document in B 64.
quotes.why_it_matters: Technical requirement for using the e-document creation APIs - file contents must be base 64 encoded

quotes.text: this is one of these business events that we have added that's called e document service status changed.
quotes.why_it_matters: Names one of the two new business events that trigger on e-document state transitions

quotes.text: the condition I have set is that the e document service status has to be exported for us to actually move forward.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows that the exported-only behavior comes from the flow's own condition, not from the business event.
